Real faces, inlined. Every sample below is the actual typeface, not a fallback — each is embedded in this page, so what you see is what would ship.

Each option changes two things together: the display face and how it is capitalised. They are not independent — a capitals face wants capitals, and a book face wants sentence case. Body copy stays Spectral throughout so only the display voice is under test.

1 Cinzel, small caps — what ships today

Roman inscriptional lettering, the open relative of the face Dark Souls uses. Titles are set in small caps because the real post titles are lowercase and Cinzel's lowercase sprawls at display size. That workaround is the tell: it is a capitals face being asked to do something it was not cut for.

The same face used as it was designed — Trajan's capitals are a capitals alphabet, and inscriptional Roman letters have no lowercase because Rome had none. Monumental, and the most confident of the five. It also shouts, and a long title in caps is genuinely slower to read.

3 Marcellus, title case — the softer Roman

Roman capitals with a humanist hand behind them — the same lineage as Cinzel but cut with real lowercase that holds at display size. Titles can be set naturally, with no caps transform and no workaround. Warmer and less severe; the trade is that it is less immediately Souls.

A book face rather than a monument, with drawn small caps instead of synthesised ones — the labels here are real small capitals, not shrunken uppercase, which is why they sit so much more quietly. Reads as a scriptorium. Least monumental of the five, and the easiest to live with over long text.

5 Spectral only, sentence case — no display face at all

The most Ash answer: delete the display face and let size, weight and space carry the whole hierarchy. One family, one voice, nothing decorative. §1 says structure carries the meaning — this is that taken literally. It is also the option with the least character, and the one that would look most like any other blog.
